summary:
Held 1 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — ASML.AS +7%, BAYN.DE +5%, DTG.DE +4%, BAB.L +3%, ASM.AS +3%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 3 downside moves (PUB.PA -5%, BRBY.L -3%, CAP.PA -3%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: ASML.AS (+6.79%) — Continuation of AI-driven semiconductor rally (Micron blowout results, analyst price-target hikes, easing MATCH Act/export-control tail risk) — no single discrete same-day headline found. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — ASML.AS is a €665B+ Euronext Amsterdam mega-cap semiconductor-equipment name; likely excluded because the uk-eu universe isn't configured to include AEX-listed megacaps or the semis-equipment sector bucket.

top_movers.catalyst: Continuation of AI-driven semiconductor rally (Micron blowout results, analyst price-target hikes, easing MATCH Act/export-control tail risk) — no single discrete same-day headline found.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ASML.AS is a €665B+ Euronext Amsterdam mega-cap semiconductor-equipment name; likely excluded because the uk-eu universe isn't configured to include AEX-listed megacaps or the semis-equipment sector bucket.
top_movers.suggestion: Add AEX index constituents (or ASML.AS specifically) to the uk-eu region universe definition so semiconductor-equipment mega-caps are eligible for momentum/mean-reversion screening.

top_movers.catalyst: Federal judge blocked Roundup objectors' move to federal court, clearing Missouri to finalize Bayer's $7.25B glyphosate settlement, extending the Supreme Court litigation-relief rally.
top_movers.miss_reason: BAYN.DE sits outside every strategy's universe: it's a DAX pharma/agrochem conglomerate whose price action is driven by binary mass-tort legal rulings, not the technical/fundamental signals the uk-eu universe screens for.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a litigation-catalyst watchlist for DAX/CAC large-caps with scheduled court rulings, allowing a reduced-size entry when a favorable ruling is confirmed same-session, instead of blanket-excluding legal-risk names.

top_movers.catalyst: No same-day news catalyst found; DTG.DE (Daimler Truck) has been trading in a volatile band on ongoing US heavy-truck tariff exposure and analyst target revisions (avg PT ~€46), but no July 1-specific trigger surfaced.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — DTG.DE is a German DAX-listed heavy-industrial/truck-manufacturing large-cap, a sector/category likely excluded from the uk-eu universe's sector allowlist (e.g. financials/consumer/tech-weighted lists that skip auto & capital-goods names).
top_movers.suggestion: Add DAX-40 industrial/auto-sector constituents (or a market-cap > €10B threshold override) to the uk-eu universe refresh so large European industrials like DTG.DE aren't structurally excluded by sector tag.

top_movers.catalyst: UK government unveiled a ~$20B defense spending increase, lifting the whole FTSE aerospace/defense complex (BAE, Babcock, Chemring) ~5%.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — Babcock is a UK defense/industrials large-cap, a sector commonly excluded by ESG/sin-stock screens or simply not covered by the region's tracked sector list, so no filter ever saw it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a defense/industrials sector bucket to the uk-eu universe (or a policy-news gate that admits FTSE names on sector-wide govt spending headlines) rather than relying solely on existing sector inclusions.

top_movers.catalyst: Read-through from Samsung/SK Hynix's ~$516B new fab capex plans lifted chip-equipment names sector-wide (ASML +6.8%); no ASM.AS-specific news, next earnings not until 2026-07-28.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ASM.AS is a large-cap (~EUR40B+) Dutch semiconductor deposition/ALD equipment maker on Euronext Amsterdam; uk-eu universes likely track ASML as the sole chip-equipment proxy and never added its equipment-basket peers.
top_movers.suggestion: Add ASM.AS to the uk-eu semiconductor-equipment basket alongside ASML so correlated capex-driven pops (Samsung/SK Hynix-style fab announcements) are captured, not just the single-name ASML slot.

top_movers.catalyst: No single fresh news item on 07-01; continued melt-up after Jun 18 Investor Day guidance raise (rev target to €1.7-2.2B, margin floor to 45%) plus fresh analyst hikes (JPMorgan to €342, Barclays to €270) on AI/hybrid-bonding optimism.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BESI.AS is a Euronext Amsterdam semiconductor-equipment name; the uk-eu universe is likely built from a static large-cap/sector list (banks, energy, consumer) that excludes semi-equipment tickers, or an ADV/cap screen not yet refreshed to reflect its 92%+ 6-month rally.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a monthly market-cap/ADV re-screen for Euronext-listed names so recent big gainers like BESI.AS (now ~€24B cap, +135% YoY) get pulled into the uk-eu universe instead of relying on a stale static list.

top_movers.catalyst: Mechanical ex-dividend adjustment: PUB.PA went ex-div for EUR 3.75/share (~4.3% of prior close) on 2026-07-01, payable 2026-07-03 — not a genuine sell-off.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (mid/large-cap French media/adtech, euro-denominated Paris listing). Even if watched, a news-reactive/momentum bot correctly ignores this since the 'loss' is a scheduled corporate-action price adjustment, not tradeable alpha.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an ex-dividend filter to the universe/loser screen that nets out announced dividend amounts from close-to-close returns so mechanical ex-div drops aren't flagged as movers or chased as mean-reversion candidates.

top_movers.catalyst: Handelsblatt reported Höttges is exploring folding T-Mobile US into a holding structure (SpaceX IPO-linked); expiry of buyback tranche 2 (30 Jun) and Starlink mobile-competition fears drove shares to a 52-week low.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — DTE.DE is a DAX40 mega-cap telecom, likely excluded because universes are scoped to UK/US large-caps or specific sectors that don't include German-listed telecoms; the decline was also a multi-day grind (buyback support removal) rather than a single sharp gap a news-reactive bot
top_movers.suggestion: Add DAX40 constituents (or German large-cap telecom) to the mean-reversion/momentum universe, and add a 'buyback-expiry' flag that surfaces names losing repurchase-driven support as mean-reversion candidates.

top_movers.catalyst: No dated news catalyst found for 2026-07-01; likely profit-taking / sector pullback after Burberry's sharp turnaround rally and recent FTSE 100 re-entry.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BRBY.L likely still excluded as a recently-reinstated FTSE 100 name (universe membership lists lag index changes) or filtered out under a luxury/consumer-discretionary sector cap.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a same-day index-membership refresh so newly re-added FTSE 100/350 constituents (like BRBY.L's re-entry) are picked up into the uk-eu universe without waiting for the next scheduled universe rebuild.

top_movers.catalyst: No fresh company news; continuation of IT-services sector derating (post-Accenture guidance cut, AI-spend fears) pushing CAP.PA to fresh 52-week lows.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — likely excluded as a non-US/UK-EU-listed IT-services large cap without a dedicated Euronext Paris tech coverage bucket, so no filter ever evaluated it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add CAC 40 IT-services names (CAP.PA, ATO.PA, TEP.PA) to a euro-tech universe with a sector-momentum gate keyed off Accenture/Concentrix guidance revisions.
